newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Dec 4.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Dec. 4:
WASHINGTON - The District of Columbia council voted to lower welfare benefits for city residents by five percent.
WASHINGTON - Maryland would become the first state to require drug tests for all welfare applicants under a proposal endorsed by a legislative panel.
WASHINGTON - A federal grand jury indicted three former officials of the giant agricultural company Archer Daniels Midland Co. on criminal price-fixing charges.
WASHINGTON - A judge in Hawaii ruled that the state may not prohibit same-sex marriages, giving new visibility to an emotional issue that has reverberated across the country.

OMAHA, NEBRASKA - Retired Air Force General George Lee Butler, once commander in chief of America's nuclear arsenal, now describes U.S. nuclear policy as "fundamentally irrational" on grounds that such arms posed a great threat to mankind.
WASHINGTON - The Justice Department barred as suspected war criminals 16 Japanese who served in the Japanese imperial army during the Second World War.
